articles.title: Carousel Gallery: Showcasing the CSS Carousel Specs
articles.description: These are completely JavaScript-free examples that use properties like overscroll-behavior, scroll-snap-type, anchor-name, and so forth. You can also check out this configurator that helps you build one and visualize how the code works. Note, these features are currently available in Chrome 135+ and other Chromium-based browsers.
articles.author: Adam Argyle

articles.title: 🎂 Celebrating 20 Years of MDN
articles.description: After two decades the MDN resource is now home to over 14,000 pages of documentation covering some 18,000 features. It’s a comprehensive and valuable resource for us all — long may it continue. (Oh, and Google sent a cake.)
articles.author: Joe Walker

articles.title: Brick by Brick: Help Us Build CSS Masonry
articles.description: Yes, issues surrounding the CSS masonry specification and syntax still remain, but you can now test things in Chrome and Edge 140 (behind a flag). This post dives deep into how it can be used, and asks for our feedback.
articles.author: Brosset & Maher

articles.title: Making a Masonry Layout That Works Today
articles.description: In relation to the above — there’s been plenty of back and forth on the new syntax to make creating masonry style layouts easier to create with CSS. But we’re not yet at a point where a final, universal decision has been made — as such, Zell shares what we can actually do right now, no flags required (thanks to a touch as JS).
articles.author: Zell Liew

articles.title: ▶  Responsive Video is (Almost) Easy Now
articles.description: A solid write up on all the things you’ll want to consider when approaching adding native video to your site, including serving both vertical and horizontal versions when context requires it.
articles.author: Koos Looijesteijn

articles.title: Making Sense of the Performance Extensibility API
articles.description: The Performance Extensibility API allows us to create custom tracks in Chrome DevTools’ Performance panel — here’s how to make use of it.
articles.author: Harry Roberts

articles.title: Creating a 'Scroll-Spy' with 2 Lines of CSS
articles.description: There’s a new CSS feature landing in Chrome 140 that lets you easily create a trackable table of contents. This effect can be achieved with a new CSS property called scroll-target-group combined with the :target-current pseudo class.
articles.author: Una Kravets

articles.title: When is WebAssembly Going to Get DOM Support?
articles.description: Working with the DOM from JavaScript is straightforward, but WebAssembly requires (a lot of) glue code to do it. Is this going to change? Daniel of the TC39 committee digs into the issue here and says that modern build toolchains and WASM’s evolution are making things easier all the time.
articles.author: Daniel Ehrenberg

articles.title: Liquid Glass on the Web
articles.description: Apple’s various operating systems will get a new, universal design aesthetic this fall, but before that roll out here’s how some developers are attempting to bring this new look to the web now.
articles.author: Chris Coyier

articles.title: Web Components: Working With Shadow DOM
articles.description: A look at how Shadow DOM fits into the broader Web Components picture, explaining why it matters, when to use it, and how to apply it effectively.
articles.author: Russell Beswick

articles.title: World Clock Slider
articles.description: This is a really smart clock component in which you can check the time in various global cities — just move the slider to see it in action. A super smooth demo, and it has a nice dark mode too.
articles.author: Jon Kantner codepen

articles.title: StaticSearch: Add Search Functionality to Any Static Site
articles.description: This solution relies on JavaScript along with data stored as JSON, so there’s no server tech needed. Usable with any static site tool but originally designed for Publican. Full docs are here.
articles.author: Craig Buckler

articles.title: Introducing Quickstrom: High-Confidence Browser Testing
articles.description: A new autonomous testing tool for the web. It claims it can find problems in “any type of web application that renders to the DOM”.
articles.author: Oskar Wickström

articles.title: Oklchroma: A Color Pattern Generator to Create Harmonious Color Scales in the OKLCH Color Space
articles.description: Provide a base color and the tool will generate a full palette, with copy/paste CSS, using a trigonometric function to, as the author explains, “adjust the Chroma as a sort of an easing wave”.
articles.author: Brecht De Ruyte

articles.title: FossFLOW: Make Beautiful Isometric Infrastructure Diagrams
articles.description: You can use the tool here. One of the neat features is the ability to insert a node then update the icon’s appearance from a variety of tech categories. There also options to save, load, import diagrams, etc.
articles.author: stan smith

articles.title: difit: A CLI Tool to View Local Git Diffs with a GitHub-Style Viewer
articles.description: You can view in the terminal or use the web UI. Also allows you to add comments to diffs and copy them with file paths and line numbers for use with AI tools.
articles.author: yoshiko

articles.title: 7.css: A Design System for Building Faithful Recreations of Classic UIs
articles.description: The style is similar to Windows 7 – hence the name – and built on top of XP.css which takes a Windows XP style approach. We’ve shared before, but it’s just been updated.
articles.author: Khang Nguyen Duy
